# User flow: sign-up to first saved recipe (Larder)

Evidence: assumption-based (only docs/PRD.md and four stub routes; no research with people)
AI use: The agent drafted the flow, states and exits from the PRD and the route stubs. A product designer reviews them and decides the open questions.
Analyst: product designer

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  signup[Sign up /signup] -->|email| verify[Check your inbox /verify-email]
  signup -->|Google| pantry
  verify -->|link ok| pantry[Pantry setup /onboarding/pantry]
  verify -.->|browse unverified| browse([Browse only, save blocked])
  pantry -->|save or skip| box[Empty recipe box]
  box --> add[Add recipe /recipes/new]
  add -->|saved| done([First recipe saved])
  add -->|not verified| verify
```

| Step | States to handle | Exits |
|---|---|---|
| Sign up (`app/signup/page.tsx`) | empty form, validation error, email already registered, submitting, network error with input kept, Google cancelled | email: verify; Google: pantry; existing account: sign in; leave |
| Verify email (`app/verify-email/page.tsx`) | waiting, resend sent or throttled, link expired or used, verified in another tab | verified: pantry; wrong address: sign up; browse unverified |
| Pantry setup (`app/onboarding/pantry/page.tsx`) | list loading, list failed, none selected, save failed | save or skip: recipe box |
| Empty recipe box (no route yet) | first-use empty, loading, load failed | add first recipe; navigate away |
| Add recipe (`app/recipes/new/page.tsx`) | blank, URL importing, import failed or partial, validation error, save failed, unverified | saved: first success; unverified: verify; cancel: box |

## Recommendations

1. Offer pantry setup after the first saved recipe; it does not help save one. Basis: judgment.
2. Keep the draft recipe when the unverified save block sends the user to verify. Basis: judgment.

## Assumptions to test

| Assumption | How to test |
|---|---|
| Pantry setup before the first recipe causes drop-off | Usability test both orders and compare completion |
| Google sign-ups need no separate verification | Check the provider's verified-email claim |

How this was made: no shell, so detect.mjs did not run and the team file was not read; built-in routes were used. A browser on the running app would let steps be marked observed.

Next: /user-interface:design takes this flow and designs each screen and its states.

Here is the flow from docs/PRD.md and the four routes under app/. The pages are stubs, so the transitions come from the PRD.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Sign-up /signup] -->|email| B[Verify email /verify-email]
  A -->|Google| C
  B --> C[Pantry setup /onboarding/pantry]
  C -->|save or skip| D[Empty recipe box]
  D --> E[Add recipe /recipes/new]
  E -->|saved| F([First recipe saved])
```

1. **Sign-up** (`/signup`): email and password, or Google.
   - States: empty, invalid email or weak password, email already taken, submitting, server error, Google cancelled.
   - Exits: success goes to verify (Google skips it); already registered goes to sign in; the visitor can leave.
2. **Verify email** (`/verify-email`)
   - States: waiting for the link, resend sent, resend throttled, link expired, link already used.
   - Exits: verified goes to pantry setup; an unverified user may browse but cannot save; a wrong address goes back to sign-up.
3. **Pantry setup** (`/onboarding/pantry`), optional
   - States: staples loading, list failed, nothing picked, saving, save failed.
   - Exits: save or skip both lead to the empty recipe box.
4. **Empty recipe box** (no route exists yet)
   - States: first-use empty with "Add your first recipe", loading, failed to load.
   - Exits: add a recipe; navigate elsewhere.
5. **Add recipe** (`/recipes/new`): paste a URL or type it
   - States: blank, importing, import failed, partial import, missing required fields, saving, save failed.
   - Exits: saved is first success; an unverified user is sent to verify; cancel returns to the box.

Screen layout, wording and visual styling are screen design work for later.
